text:
sara: FYI customer Clipper just escalated — they see a huge spike in 502s and timeouts hitting hosted inference in eu3-az starting ~09:15 UTC. They included a sample request id: req_3f9b.

infra-bot: ALERT: hosted-inference.eu3 5xx spike detected 09:14-09:28 (5xx rate 4.9% avg) — auto-created incident #INC-2026-443.

mike: @sara thanks. Do we have any network alerts for eu3 around 09:10-09:25? traceroutes or tcpdump from edge nodes? any path changes?

lee: seeing unusual signs on our eu3 egress to ISP-Blue. BGP next-hop flipped at 09:12 and we started observing ECN-marked packets + MSS fragmentation. Captured a short tcpdump showing retransmits/dup acks.

```
# /tmp/tcpdump-snippet
09:13:02.123 IP 10.0.4.22.443 > 10.8.1.12.53892: Flags [.], seq 3456:4321, ack 129, win 64240, options [nop,nop,TS val 123456 ecr 654321], length 865
09:13:02.125 IP 10.8.1.12.53892 > 10.0.4.22.443: Flags [R.], seq 129, ack 3456, win 0, length 0
09:13:02.130 IP 10.0.4.22 > 10.8.1.12: ICMP frag-needed mtu=1400
```

lee: pings to peer show ~2.1% packet loss and 30-120ms jitter during the window. Likely MTU mismatch + ECN/DSCP handling on their new path.

emily: Customer says their bulk inference batch jobs are failing mid-run; they also saw intermittent auth 401s immediately before 502 bursts (could be retries stacking). They're asking for RCA and billing credit — they were billed for retries.

mike: mitigation we applied: (1) temporarily routed affected traffic to eu3-b fallback pool (eu3b), (2) applied MTU clamp to egress nodes and disabled ECN on the proxy tier: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_ecn=0` + `ip link set mtu 1400 dev eth0` on nodes serving eu3-edge, (3) rolling restart proxies in 5s stagger.

lee: provider (ISP-Blue) acknowledged a maintenance-induced path shift; they say a middlebox on the new path mishandles ECN and large frames. They pushed a short-term fix to respect PMTU and will revert route flip in next 45m. Current loss down to ~0.3% after clamp.

sara: customer confirmed error rate dropped and jobs resumed after our mitigation. They report 502s reduced to near-zero for the last 15m. They asked that we leave the clamp for 2 hours then test. :thumbsup:

emily: opened support case CS-4578 for billing adjustment and customer escalation notes. Added timeline + sample request ids.

mike: follow-ups: we should add BGP path-change alerting for eu3 (threshold: >1 ASPATH change/min for 5m), add MTU/ECN health checks on egress monitors, and consider automated per-customer fallback to dedicated pools when 5xx spikes exceed X. Tagging @product for console flag feature.

lee: saved full pcap to internal S3 path s3://redwood-incidents/1715678901-eu3-gre-ecn/ and uploaded router RIB snapshots to /var/logs/rib-dumps/1715678901.

infra-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated 10:05 UTC — routing + MTU clamp applied. Monitoring continuing for 2h.

mike: notes for postmortem: root cause appears to be a provider-side route shift causing a new path with a device that incorrectly handles ECN/MMTU leading to fragmentation/ICMP frag-needed and retransmits. Secondary effects: client retries and transient auth failures -> increased 5xx surface. Action items assigned to @lee (liaise with ISP-Blue & collect RIB/pcap), @emily (customer billing case), @sara (customer comms).

sara: I'll send the customer a summary and ETA for PMTU removal tests. Closing thread when monitoring window ends.
